editorial.headline: Electric Motor Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27111 covers the making of electric motors and core components, with a clear national PMA opening and a firm Bali registration block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27111 is the industrial code for making electric motors and the parts that make those motors work. The slim record defines the activity around electric motor production and its components or parts, including alternating-current motors, direct-current motors, dynamo armatures, stators, rotors, brushes, and commutators. It expressly excludes internal combustion engines used to start motors. In plain English, this is a manufacturing classification for the physical production of electric motor systems and their essential electromechanical components, not a general trading, repair, or combustion-engine category.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to micro, small, medium, and large businesses, so the code is not reserved only for heavy industrial operators. A small workshop making components and a larger manufacturing operation can both sit within the same activity description, provided the real business activity is the manufacture of the electric motors or listed parts themselves. That matters because the code is defined by what is being made: AC motors, DC motors, armatures, stators, rotors, brushes, commutators, and related components or parts.

Nationally, the foreign-investment reading is straightforward. The PMA status is marked as TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. On the national rule set alone, this is therefore a foreign-open manufacturing activity with no lower foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the slim record. For founders reading the code from Jakarta or from the national investment list, the key takeaway is simple: the record treats KBLI 27111 as open to full foreign ownership at the national level.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks the Bali status as BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a soft caveat. A foreign investor may see a nationally open, 100% PMA-eligible activity, but cannot register this PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali moratorium recorded here.
